## §401b. Strikes 1–3 on the page — his first four verdicts on strike 1, and the bass clarinet's order (2026-09-11 late, Fable 5.1)

**His words, on seeing strike 1:** *"the short notes with gcs don't have duration lines, take note and remove them from strike 1; can you right justify tongue ram and make sure there is a space between tongue and ram there may be the gc may be in the way; center (slap) and jete better please; and can you look into the vertical order for bcl is it dot accent + or dot + accent, or something else; lets do the 1st 3 strikes and pls put the staff lines to the end of the page; and midi playback? defered for when you do more?"*

**Done, all registry data plus two small code paths:**
- **No duration brick on a strike** — `brick: false` in byEnv.strike and the four byTechnique strike entries. STANDING RULE, his: a short note with a GC has no duration line.
- **Text alignment per technique** — `instrAlign` (start | middle | end) on the head column: tongue ram `end` (right edge at the head's right edge, clear of the go line and the GC's landing), (slap) and jeté `middle`. layout passes `anchor`, render writes `text-anchor` and `xml:space="preserve"` (the space between "tongue" and "ram" was being swallowed by the GC's arc over it, not by the font; preserved now either way).
- **Staff lines to the page edge in every view** — `engraving.render.staffFull: true` (render honoured it only as a notation-view option; the tuba's day-22 verdict cut the staff at the material's end; false = the tuba look).

**The bass clarinet's column, from the head outward: dot · > · + · fff · (slap).** Gould (Behind Bars, "combining articulation marks", from memory — the search found nothing quotable): staccato and tenuto nearest the notehead, accents next, technique signs (harmonic ○, stopped +, snap pizz, bowing) outermost of the articulations, then dynamics. What the page draws is that order. The same holds for the violins' snap-pizz circle: dot · > · ○ · fff.

**MIDI playback — deferred, and here is the honest state:** the notation app's player is the tuba's, ported byte-exact (0g); its per-part ports and channels for the septet (D11's curve channels, the piano's two tracks) are unverified, and the AI's browser hears nothing (NITS). ## §401e. Piece #2's rules surfaced — stems, and where the chrome sits; the piano's GC made a single lane's size, landing between the staves (2026-09-11 late, Fable 5.1)

**His words** (with a crop of #2's page: a low bass cluster, stem down, flag, fff under the flag; and a tremolo note with + and an accent below): *"so stems up or down, there is a rule in 2pno, try to find it, also rule there about where to position all of the accents, dynamics etc, lets see if we can surface all of it and then since this grand staff is double height Let's make the GC the same height as all the other GCs in the other parts. and let's make the impact in the middle of the staff ... the top of the arc at the very top of the lane ... wherever the impact lands between the two staffs."*

**#2's rules, from its own code** (`tools/notation_studio/engine/translators/pluckedPianoChord.js` `_autoClefAndStem`, session 63; `engine/idioms/pluckedPianoChord.js` steps 7–8; `idioms/percussionCellMotive.js` line 215; dims: `verticalSpacing.standardSs` 0.45, `stem.flagClearance.clearanceSs` 1.0):
- **Stem direction (piano):** all notes in the bass range → bass clef, stem **UP**; all treble → treble clef, stem **DOWN**; mixed → treble, down. I.e. by staff position, the classical way — not reversed. (The v1 idiom was down-only; up came in session 58c.)
- **Above the chord:** the text instruction (*pizz.*) 0.45 ss above the highest chord element (stem-down) or above the STEM TIP (stem-up); an accent (`scriptAbove`) goes above too; the ottava outermost above.
- **Below the chord:** the dynamic 0.45 ss below the STEM TIP (stem-down → under the flag) or below the lowest notehead (stem-up); *Ped.* below the dynamic.
- **The 'none' (stemless) rule:** chrome anchors lift/drop to the STAFF LINE when the chord sits inside the staff.
- **Percussion cells:** articulations on the head side, opposite the stem (+ and the accent below a stem-up note — his crop's second cell).
- **Against the septet's strike look now:** stems all UP (mine, §401, to keep the chain off the flag); dot · > (· symbol) · fff · text all on the head side below (the tuba's stackBelow, Gould). #2 would put the accent and text ABOVE and the dynamic under the flag. **His call — not changed.**

**The piano's GC:** `GC.systemOf(view, part)` = the first staff's system of a multi-staff part (its top is the lane's top, its bottom the boundary between the staves, its height one lane's), else the part's lane; ONE copy used by render.js (arc + impact) and animobj.js (the ball), so the ball lands on the marker. The go line keeps the whole lane (§401d). Tests: septet 86 GREEN; staged render / animobj / layout GREEN.

Measured first: the rule engages past `glyphs.standards.ottava.ledgerLineThreshold` ledger lines, which the tuba set to **4** (layout's comment still says 3); that head sits at y −6 = the 4th ledger, inside the tuba's rule. The piano's upper staff "worked" because its two ottavas were beyond 4. Decided: `engraving.layout.ottavaLedgerThreshold: 3` in the septet's container (piece #2's staff-router rule, Gould's) — read by layout ahead of the shared glyph standard, so the tuba pages keep their 4 (staged layout battery GREEN) and every septet part, both piano staves, gets the ottava from the 4th ledger line on. ## §401k. The grand staff's gap — the standard found, and made data: 6 ss, the piano lane re-weighted (2026-09-11 late, Fable 5.1)

**His words:** *"look at the 2pno piece and see if we have in rules or standards about the vertical Space between the two piano staffs. The septet one looks too big ... let's see if we can nail down a standard ... then adjust the piano grand staff size ... and then readjust the lane size for all the other ones ... see if there's a standard spacing ... even if Lilly Pond has engraving rules ... they are just the same distance as between any other staff. I don't think that's generally how it's done."*

**Looked up, not guessed:**
- **Piece #2:** `dimensions_table.json` `grandStaff.interStaffGap = 6 ss` — treble bottom line → bass top line — LOCKED (D.9.1, 2026-05-05), re-measured off its LilyPond reference `Ostinato_L-B2-Ef3-E3_R-G4-Gs4-C5.svg`; the hand-seeded 8 was corrected to LP's 6. `COORDS.md`: the grand staff's midline = `(trebleBot + bassTop) / 2`.
- **LilyPond 2.24.4 itself** (`scm/lily/define-grobs.scm`, StaffGrouper): within a PianoStaff/GrandStaff `staff-staff-spacing basic-distance 9` centre-to-centre = a **5 ss** gap (minimum 7 = 3 ss, padding 1); between different instruments `staffgroup-staff-spacing basic-distance 10.5` = 6.5 ss. So the piano's staves sit closer than two players' — his instinct was right.
- **The septet before:** each staff centred in its own half of a weight-2 lane → **12.46 ss** gap, the same as between two parts (12.96).

**Built:** registry `engraving.layout.grandStaff.interStaffGapSs: 6` (#2's locked value; LP's 5 is one number away) · `coords.withStaves(systems, stavesOf, opts)` places a part's staves at that gap centred in the lane — each keeps its half-lane band (the GC's impact stays at the gap's middle) and carries a `midFrac` the view honours for its middle line; the fraction derives from the lane's own ss scale, so the same 6 holds in the video frame, the zoom and any export · the app passes it at both view builders · the piano's weight 2 → **1.576** so its outer air equals a player's lane (lane = unit + 4 + 6 ss → u = 17.37 ss, the six other lanes +5.5 %). Tests: septet 86 GREEN, coords GREEN. The exporters do not split staves yet (NITS, still ten-lane).

## §401l. Ottava brackets — Gould's rule kept, the hook past the ledger overhang (2026-09-11 late, Fable 5.1)

**His words:** *"look up bracket rules and tell me and see if they change 8ve brackets, ideally they would span past the ledger line of note head and dynamic etc"* — then, offered A (Gould + clear the ledger overhang and the accidental) · B (span the whole column) · C (sign alone for a single note): *"a but depends what side right? accidental on right if 8va is on top"*.

Gould (from memory; nothing quotable found online): the sign at the first affected note, left edge aligned with the notehead or its accidental; the dotted line to the last note's right edge; a short hook toward the staff; a single note may carry the sign alone; the sign outermost on its side. The accidental is always LEFT of the head, so the two ends do not depend on the side: the sign clears the accidental (already: `dx0Ss = leftEdgeDx`), the hook now clears the ledger line's overhang on the right (`dx1Ss` += the ledger extension when the note has ledgers) — 8va above or 8vb below alike. B (spanning the dynamic) and C are not Gould and were not chosen. Tests: septet 86 GREEN; the tuba layout battery GREEN (its snapshot page has no ledgered ottava… or the change is inside its tolerance — either way unchanged).

## §401m. The ottava's hook: rightmost ink + the smallest gap; the "pie wedge" that was not one (2026-09-11 late, Fable 5.1)

**His words:** *"looks like this one aligns with stem so flush with notehead right; The second one might line up on the ledger. Let's find a standard ... the rightmost thing plus a small gap ... the smallest gap would be the gap between the staccato dot and the notehead ... the second image seems to reveal that the pie wedge animation is creeping back in. We had this trouble in the tuba score too. Just make sure those are hidden or shut off."*

- **The standard, looked up:** LilyPond's `OttavaBracket` `shorten-pair (-0.8 . -0.6)` — the bracket runs 0.8 ss LEFT of the first note and **0.6 ss past the last note's right edge**; `padding 0.5`, `staff-padding 2.0`, dashed. Gould: "a little beyond" the last note. **His rule, as data:** `engraving.layout.ottavaEndGapSs: 0.15` = the staccato-dot gap (the three gaps in the registry: tight 0.15 · medium 0.3 · standard 0.45) past the rightmost ink — the head, or the ledger line's overhang. The left end already sits at the accidental's left edge.
- **The circle:** measured, not assumed — no object in 0–12 s carries a follower trigger (no `morphBend`, no envelope, no hold ≥ 3 s), and `motivePie` has been OFF since the tuba's day 24. The wedge could not have drawn. The blue ring in his crop is the notation page's own SELECTION ring (2d.6: click a note to select it for G beaming; ESC clears) — he had clicked that note. Done anyway, so it can never creep: the collector honours `enabled: false` for EVERY animated kind (the tuba's per-kind cure, generalised) and `lineWedge` is OFF in the registry for this piece. `test_animobj` — its lineWedge assertion runs with the switch forced on, as the pie's does.
